_about: The tools/list a server serves for tools that subscribe and tools that don't (design §2.4, §2.12, §3). Each scenario defines the events and vendor tools named, attaches with the given builtin_tools (null: the defaults; subscribe, list and unsubscribe on, wait off) on an enabled client (a valid key) or a disabled one (no key), and asks tools/list. The app's name (GET /app) is "Crawler". Run every scenario twice per server type: once registering each tool that subscribes through the attachment (TS attached.registerTool, Python @attached.tool, Go wakeshift.AddTool / mcpgo.AddTool) and once registering it with the host SDK and naming it in wrap (TS wake.attach(server, { wrap }), Python wrap=, Go AttachOptions.Wrap); both must give the same tools_list. get_page (subscribes: null) is always registered with the host SDK directly and never named in wrap. check_crawl has subscribes: [] (a tool that subscribes to nothing). Compare tools by name (order isn't pinned: go-sdk sorts tools/list itself); compare description exactly, and inputSchema and outputSchema after the shape normalization in README.md (per property: type, description, enum; required sorted; top-level type); a tool without outputSchema must serve none. annotations are compared exactly; a vendor tool here has none. Wakeshift's arguments are never required. list_subscriptions lists session_key, as unsubscribe_events does: without identify it lists the calling conversation's subscriptions. list_subscriptions and unsubscribe_events are listed only when one of the server's tools is declared with subscribes that name an event (registered or wrap; subscribes: [] doesn't count) or an event is open to subscribe_events. builtin_tools false (Python False, Go BuiltinTools{DisableAll: true}) turns every built-in off.
_status: FINAL (compact tools/list bench, 2026-11-05: compact matched or beat the baseline in every cell). compact_strings in subscribing-tools-list.json is the one place these strings live; every literal that uses them (wake-args.json compact, subscribes.json compact_cases, event-tools.json, events-list.json tools, subscribing-tools-list.json scenarios, tool-output-schemas.json) is generated from it.
_c1_dependent: Which events reach subscribe_events (only personal, authorize or public ones) is the SDK's own rule and holds without C1; the core refusing the same (C1) isn't visible in tools/list.
